Model3_Bayes_Renewable_Energy1

Default Baseline Model

# load packages
library(brms)
## Loading required package: Rcpp
## Loading 'brms' package (version 2.23.0). Useful instructions
## can be found by typing help('brms'). A more detailed introduction
## to the package is available through vignette('brms_overview').
## 
## Attaching package: 'brms'
## The following object is masked from 'package:stats':
## 
##     ar
library(ggplot2)

# set seed
set.seed(42)

# set cores
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())

# set path
data_path <- "data/World_Energy_Consumption.csv"

# set model constants
year_use <- 2018
target <- "renewables_share_energy"
features <- c(
  "gas_share_elec",
  "fossil_elec_per_capita",
  "coal_share_energy",
  "energy_per_gdp",
  "energy_per_capita"
)
# read data
energy <- read.csv(data_path)

# keep 2018 sovereign countries
energy_2018 <- energy[
  energy$year == year_use &
    !is.na(energy$iso_code) &
    nchar(energy$iso_code) == 3,
]

# keep needed columns
energy_2018 <- energy_2018[, c("country", "iso_code", features, target)]

# drop missing rows
energy_2018 <- na.omit(energy_2018)

# reset row names
rownames(energy_2018) <- NULL

# print checks
cat("year:", year_use, "\n")
## year: 2018
cat("countries with complete data:", nrow(energy_2018), "\n")
## countries with complete data: 69
cat("features:\n")
## features:
print(features)
## [1] "gas_share_elec"         "fossil_elec_per_capita" "coal_share_energy"     
## [4] "energy_per_gdp"         "energy_per_capita"
cat("target:", target, "\n")
## target: renewables_share_energy
# preview data
head(energy_2018)
##      country iso_code gas_share_elec fossil_elec_per_capita coal_share_energy
## 1    Algeria      DZA         91.262               1701.052             0.868
## 2  Argentina      ARG         64.211               2213.511             1.393
## 3  Australia      AUS         20.026               8304.900            31.307

## 6 Bangladesh      BGD         72.269                443.293             6.636

## 4          1.068         46186.543                  34.528
## 5          1.069         16897.240                   3.066
## 6          0.627          2630.028                   0.707
# check dimensions
dim(energy_2018)
## [1] 69  8
# check country count
length(unique(energy_2018$country))
## [1] 69
# check missing values
colSums(is.na(energy_2018))
##                 country                iso_code          gas_share_elec 
##                       0                       0                       0 
##  fossil_elec_per_capita       coal_share_energy          energy_per_gdp 
##                       0                       0                       0 
##       energy_per_capita renewables_share_energy 
##                       0                       0
# check target summary
summary(energy_2018[[target]])
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##   0.007   5.750   9.424  14.364  20.762  69.601
sd(energy_2018[[target]])
## [1] 13.09883
# make scaled copy
energy_scaled <- energy_2018

# scale predictors
energy_scaled[, features] <- scale(energy_2018[, features])

# preview scaled data
head(energy_scaled)
##      country iso_code gas_share_elec fossil_elec_per_capita coal_share_energy
## 1    Algeria      DZA      2.2992172             -0.4688117        -0.9284556
## 2  Argentina      ARG      1.2843137             -0.2425767        -0.8975282
## 3  Australia      AUS     -0.3734258              2.4465851         0.8646908

## 5 Azerbaijan      AZE      1.0771760             -0.2653066        -0.9792945
## 6 Bangladesh      BGD      1.5866350             -1.0240738        -0.5886656
##   energy_per_gdp energy_per_capita renewables_share_energy
## 1    -0.30474506        -0.7899899                   0.288
## 2    -0.22911203        -0.5445507                  11.332
## 3    -0.05073225         1.1562804                   8.278
## 4    -0.39892959         0.4076792                  34.528
## 5    -0.39750255        -0.7532793                   3.066
## 6    -1.02825348        -1.3187978                   0.707
# check scaled predictor means
round(colMeans(energy_scaled[, features]), 6)
##         gas_share_elec fossil_elec_per_capita      coal_share_energy 
##                      0                      0                      0 
##         energy_per_gdp      energy_per_capita 
##                      0                      0
# check scaled predictor sds
apply(energy_scaled[, features], 2, sd)
##         gas_share_elec fossil_elec_per_capita      coal_share_energy 
##                      1                      1                      1 
##         energy_per_gdp      energy_per_capita 
##                      1                      1
# define formula
energy_formula <- renewables_share_energy ~
  gas_share_elec +
  fossil_elec_per_capita +
  coal_share_energy +
  energy_per_gdp +
  energy_per_capita

# inspect default priors
energy_prior <- default_prior(
  energy_formula,
  data = energy_scaled,
  family = gaussian()
)

energy_prior
##                    prior     class                   coef group resp dpar nlpar
##                   (flat)         b                                             
##                   (flat)         b      coal_share_energy                      
##                   (flat)         b      energy_per_capita                      
##                   (flat)         b         energy_per_gdp                      
##                   (flat)         b fossil_elec_per_capita                      
##                   (flat)         b         gas_share_elec                      
##  student_t(3, 9.4, 10.4) Intercept                                             
##    student_t(3, 0, 10.4)     sigma                                             
##  lb ub tag       source
##                 default
##            (vectorized)
##            (vectorized)
##            (vectorized)
##            (vectorized)
##            (vectorized)
##                 default
##   0             default
# fit gaussian bayesian linear regression
energy_brm <- brm(
  energy_formula,
  family = gaussian(),
  data = energy_scaled,
  chains = 4,
  cores = getOption("mc.cores", 1),
  iter = 1000,
  warmup = 180,
  thin = 1,
  prior = energy_prior
)

# get posterior predictive draws
post_preds <- posterior_predict(energy_brm)

# get posterior predictive means
energy_2018$bayes_pred_mean <- colMeans(post_preds)

# get residuals
energy_2018$bayes_residual <- energy_2018[[target]] - energy_2018$bayes_pred_mean

# get absolute residuals
energy_2018$abs_bayes_residual <- abs(energy_2018$bayes_residual)

# sort by residual
energy_results <- energy_2018[order(energy_2018$bayes_residual, decreasing = TRUE), ]

# preview top residuals
head(energy_results[, c("country", target, "bayes_pred_mean", "bayes_residual")], 10)

Adding manual priors

# get target mean for intercept prior
target_mean <- mean(energy_2018[[target]])
target_mean
## [1] 14.3637
# define manual priors
manual_prior <- c(
  prior(student_t(3, 14.367, 10), class = "Intercept"),
  prior(normal(0, 5), class = "b", coef = "gas_share_elec"),
  prior(normal(0, 5), class = "b", coef = "fossil_elec_per_capita"),
  prior(normal(0, 5), class = "b", coef = "coal_share_energy"),
  prior(normal(0, 5), class = "b", coef = "energy_per_gdp"),
  prior(normal(0, 5), class = "b", coef = "energy_per_capita"),
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 10), class = "sigma")
)
# fit manual prior model
energy_brm_manual <- brm(
  energy_formula,
  family = gaussian(),
  data = energy_scaled,
  chains = 4,
  cores = getOption("mc.cores", 1),
  iter = 4000,
  warmup = 720,
  thin = 1,
  prior = manual_prior
)

##          total post-warmup draws = 13120
## 
## Regression Coefficients:
##                        Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Rhat Bulk_ESS
## Intercept                 14.37      1.06    12.29    16.50 1.00    14185
## gas_share_elec            -7.26      1.49   -10.14    -4.28 1.00     5643
## fossil_elec_per_capita    -3.24      1.59    -6.38    -0.11 1.00     6063
## coal_share_energy         -4.85      1.61    -7.99    -1.71 1.00     5482
## energy_per_gdp            -1.45      1.45    -4.27     1.39 1.00     6636
## energy_per_capita          3.41      1.73     0.01     6.80 1.00     5138
##                        Tail_ESS
## Intercept                  9402
## gas_share_elec             8457
## fossil_elec_per_capita     8567
## coal_share_energy          8035
## energy_per_gdp             9429
## energy_per_capita          7806
## 
## Further Distributional Parameters:
##       Estimate Est.Error l-95% CI u-95% CI Rhat Bulk_ESS Tail_ESS
## sigma     8.94      0.80     7.53    10.65 1.00    12714    10032
## 
## Draws were sampled using sampling(NUTS). For each parameter, Bulk_ESS
## and Tail_ESS are effective sample size measures, and Rhat is the potential
## scale reduction factor on split chains (at convergence, Rhat = 1).

The default-prior and manual-prior models told the same overall story, which is reassuring: the main coefficient directions were stable, the same broad countries remained over and under-predicted, and the posterior diagnostics improved with the longer manual-prior run. Although the manual-prior model had a slightly lower Bayesian R2 than the default-prior version, it gave a more disciplined Bayesian specification by replacing flat coefficient priors with weakly informative Normal priors and produced cleaner posterior interpretation. In particular, the manual-prior fit reduced uncertainty enough that fossil_elec_per_capita became credibly negative and energy_per_capita became credibly positive, while gas_share_elec and coal_share_energy remained clearly negative and energy_per_gdp remained uncertain. Because the manual-prior specification improves interpretability without changing the overall substantive conclusions, we move forward with it as our primary Bayesian model.

Cross Validation

# set cv constants
k_folds <- 5
cv_iter <- 4000
cv_warmup <- 720
cv_thin <- 1
# create target tiers
bins <- c(0, 5, 15, 30, 100)
labels <- c("very_low", "low", "medium", "high")

# add tiers
energy_2018$tier <- cut(energy_2018[[target]], breaks = bins, labels = labels, include.lowest = TRUE)

# check tier counts
tier_counts <- table(energy_2018$tier)
tier_counts
## 
## very_low      low   medium     high 
##       17       27       18        7
# set seed
set.seed(42)

# initialize fold vector
fold_assignments <- rep(NA_integer_, nrow(energy_2018))

# assign folds within each tier
for (tier_label in levels(energy_2018$tier)) {
  tier_idx <- which(energy_2018$tier == tier_label)
  tier_idx <- sample(tier_idx)
  
  for (i in seq_along(tier_idx)) {
    fold_assignments[tier_idx[i]] <- (i - 1) %% k_folds + 1
  }
}

# store folds
energy_2018$fold <- fold_assignments

# check fold balance
table(energy_2018$tier, energy_2018$fold)
##           
##            1 2 3 4 5
##   very_low 4 4 3 3 3
##   low      6 6 5 5 5
##   medium   4 4 4 3 3
##   high     2 2 1 1 1
# define fold fit function
fit_bayes_fold <- function(train_data, test_data, target, features, iter, warmup, thin) {
  
  # make scaled copies
  train_scaled <- train_data
  test_scaled <- test_data
  
  # scale predictors using train fold only
  train_means <- sapply(train_data[, features], mean)
  train_sds <- sapply(train_data[, features], sd)
  
  for (feat in features) {
    train_scaled[[feat]] <- (train_data[[feat]] - train_means[feat]) / train_sds[feat]
    test_scaled[[feat]] <- (test_data[[feat]] - train_means[feat]) / train_sds[feat]
  }
  
  # get train target mean
  train_target_mean <- mean(train_scaled[[target]])
  
  # define manual priors
  fold_prior <- c(
    prior(student_t(3, 14.367, 10), class = "Intercept"),
    prior(normal(0, 5), class = "b", coef = "gas_share_elec"),
    prior(normal(0, 5), class = "b", coef = "fossil_elec_per_capita"),
    prior(normal(0, 5), class = "b", coef = "coal_share_energy"),
    prior(normal(0, 5), class = "b", coef = "energy_per_gdp"),
    prior(normal(0, 5), class = "b", coef = "energy_per_capita"),
    prior(student_t(3, 0, 10), class = "sigma")
)
  
  
  # fit model
  fold_model <- brm(
    energy_formula,
    family = gaussian(),
    data = train_scaled,
    chains = 4,
    cores = getOption("mc.cores", 1),
    iter = iter,
    warmup = warmup,
    thin = thin,
    prior = fold_prior,
    refresh = 0
  )
  
  # get posterior expected draws for test fold
  fold_epred <- posterior_epred(fold_model, newdata = test_scaled)

  # get posterior expected means
  fold_pred_mean <- colMeans(fold_epred)
  
  # return outputs
  list(
    model = fold_model,
    pred_mean = fold_pred_mean,
    y_true = test_scaled[[target]]
  )
}
# initialize storage
cv_results <- list()
cv_metrics <- data.frame(
  fold = integer(),
  rmse = numeric(),
  r2 = numeric()
)

# initialize oof predictions
energy_2018$cv_bayes_pred <- NA_real_

# run cv
cat("running", k_folds, "fold cross-validation...\n\n")
## running 5 fold cross-validation...
cat(sprintf("%-6s %-16s %-12s\n", "Fold", "Val RMSE (pp)", "Val R2"))
## Fold   Val RMSE (pp)    Val R2
for (fold in 1:k_folds) {
  
  # split data
  train_data <- energy_2018[energy_2018$fold != fold, ]
  test_data <- energy_2018[energy_2018$fold == fold, ]
  
  # fit fold model
  fold_out <- fit_bayes_fold(
    train_data = train_data,
    test_data = test_data,
    target = target,
    features = features,
    iter = cv_iter,
    warmup = cv_warmup,
    thin = cv_thin
  )
  
  # get predictions
  y_pred <- fold_out$pred_mean
  y_true <- fold_out$y_true
  
  # get fold metrics
  fold_rmse <- sqrt(mean((y_pred - y_true)^2))
  fold_r2 <- 1 - sum((y_true - y_pred)^2) / sum((y_true - mean(y_true))^2)
  
  # store metrics
  cv_metrics <- rbind(
    cv_metrics,
    data.frame(
      fold = fold,
      rmse = fold_rmse,
      r2 = fold_r2
    )
  )
  
  # store oof predictions
  energy_2018$cv_bayes_pred[energy_2018$fold == fold] <- y_pred
  
  # store model object if needed
  cv_results[[paste0("fold_", fold)]] <- fold_out
  
  # print fold summary
  cat(sprintf("%-6d %-16.3f %-12.4f\n", fold, fold_rmse, fold_r2))
}

We move forward with this Bayesian model because it gives us strong out-of-sample performance while still being easy to interpret. Its cross-validated results are essentially the same as the MLP’s, which suggests the current five predictors already capture most of the predictive signal available in this setup. Because the Bayesian model matches the MLP so closely without adding extra functional complexity, we keep the simpler specification as our primary Bayesian model.

  main = "cv rmse by fold",
  xlab = "fold",
  ylab = "rmse (percentage points)",
  col = "steelblue"
)

abline(h = mean(cv_metrics$rmse), col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)

# plot r2 by fold
barplot(
  cv_metrics$r2,
  names.arg = cv_metrics$fold,
  main = "cv r2 by fold",
  xlab = "fold",
  ylab = "r2",
  col = "steelblue"
)

abline(h = mean(cv_metrics$r2), col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)

# reset layout
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
# get top and bottom residuals
top10_cv <- head(cv_energy_results, 10)
bot10_cv <- tail(cv_energy_results, 10)

# combine and sort
cv_bar_data <- rbind(top10_cv, bot10_cv)
cv_bar_data <- cv_bar_data[order(cv_bar_data$cv_bayes_residual), ]

# set colors
bar_colors <- ifelse(cv_bar_data$cv_bayes_residual > 0, "seagreen", "tomato")

# plot residual bar chart
barplot(
  cv_bar_data$cv_bayes_residual,
  names.arg = cv_bar_data$country,
  horiz = TRUE,
  las = 1,
  col = bar_colors,
  main = "top over- and under-performers",
  xlab = "actual - predicted (percentage points)"
)

abline(v = 0, lwd = 1)

# plot residual distribution
hist(
  energy_2018$cv_bayes_residual,
  breaks = 18,
  col = "steelblue",
  main = "cv residual distribution",
  xlab = "residual (percentage points)"
)

    "b_coal_share_energy",
    "b_energy_per_gdp",

  ),
  probs = c(0.025, 0.975)
)

  ),

)

# order terms

# plot intervals
plot(

)

segments(

)

# get posterior expected draws for all countries from full manual-prior model
country_epred <- posterior_epred(energy_brm_manual, newdata = energy_scaled)

# build prediction interval table
country_pred_table <- data.frame(
  country = energy_2018$country,
  actual = energy_2018[[target]],
  pred_mean = colMeans(country_epred),
  pred_lower_95 = apply(country_epred, 2, quantile, 0.025),
  pred_upper_95 = apply(country_epred, 2, quantile, 0.975)
)

# show selected countries
country_pred_table[country_pred_table$country %in% c(
  "Norway", "Brazil", "New Zealand", "Luxembourg", "France", "Hong Kong"
), ]

# get posterior predictive draws for all countries
country_post_pred <- posterior_predict(energy_brm_manual, newdata = energy_scaled)

# residual draws
residual_draws <- sweep(country_post_pred, 2, energy_2018[[target]], FUN = "-")
residual_draws <- -residual_draws

# build residual probability table
country_resid_table <- data.frame(
  country = energy_2018$country,
  actual = energy_2018[[target]],
  pred_mean = colMeans(country_post_pred),
  resid_mean = colMeans(residual_draws),
  resid_lower_95 = apply(residual_draws, 2, quantile, 0.025),
  resid_upper_95 = apply(residual_draws, 2, quantile, 0.975),
  prob_overperform = colMeans(residual_draws > 0),
  prob_underperform = colMeans(residual_draws < 0)
)

# sort by posterior mean residual
country_resid_table <- country_resid_table[order(country_resid_table$resid_mean, decreasing = TRUE), ]

# preview top and bottom

# plot posterior probability of over-performance
barplot(
  plot_data$prob_overperform,
  names.arg = plot_data$country,
  horiz = TRUE,
  las = 1,
  xlim = c(0, 1),
  col = "steelblue",

  xlab = "probability actual > predicted"
)

# build output table to match mlp csv structure
bayes_results_export <- energy_2018[, c("country", "iso_code", target, "tier")]

# use cv predictions as oof values
bayes_results_export$oof_predicted <- energy_2018$cv_bayes_pred
bayes_results_export$oof_residual <- energy_2018$cv_bayes_residual
bayes_results_export$abs_residual <- abs(energy_2018$cv_bayes_residual)

# use full manual-prior model predictions as final values
bayes_results_export$final_predicted <- energy_2018$bayes_pred_mean_manual
bayes_results_export$final_residual <- energy_2018$bayes_residual_manual

# order columns exactly like mlp output
bayes_results_export <- bayes_results_export[, c(
  "country",
  "iso_code",
  target,
  "oof_predicted",
  "oof_residual",
  "final_predicted",
  "final_residual",
  "abs_residual",
  "tier"
)]

# save csv
write.csv(
  bayes_results_export,
  "bayes_country_predictions.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
